I could not find any images of main boards that had any additional connectors, but there are conversions that can be done to convert the RF output to composite video for use with a composite monitor. This picture with the red RCA jack looks like that may be a modification. That RCA jack looks exactly like the kind Radio Shack used to sell for audio/video projects or replacements. It was a panel/chassis mount like that and later versions were available in gold plating. Given the location of the jack, it appears to be video related. I'm certain it is a modification because it mounts through the plastic case and would have required some hand assembly. The Sinclair ZX-81 was made to a specific price point and any additional parts or labor would have pushed its price out of the target range. Sir Clive was adamant it would sell for under 100 pounds and the construction shows the shortcuts they took to make that happen. There isn't even a solder mask on the PC board because that was too much unnecessary cost. So given all that, if you are not the sole owner of the machine, it may have been modified for composite video output or some other custom application. If only you owned it and you made no mods, well then you have something truly unusual there and I'd like to see inside pictures (if possible).

I think the transistor is there to inject the sync signals into the video stream, but it may also just be a way to amplify the signal enough to drive the 75 ohm impedance that BNC composite uses. The Z-80 processor was used to generate the video signal but I don't remember if it also generated the 60 Hz vertical sync and the 15.75 KHz horizontal sync used by the North American NTSC standard or if the RF modulator did that. It seems likely the processor did it since the FAST command would increase the CPU clock to 4 MHz and the video would blank out during that time. Video was only available when the SLOW command was issued. I lost a lot of typed in code when I could not get the SLOW command to take after accidentally switching to FAST mode.
